messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: HTTP 5xx spike detected on inference-gateway-prod-eu-west1. Error rate = 14.8% over the last 5m (baseline 0.2%). Top path: /v1/generate (502, 504). PagerDuty incident: <https://pd.example.com/incidents/P12345|P12345>.

pagerduty: Incident P12345 triggered by alert: INFERENCE_GATEWAY_5XX_SPIKE. Escalation policy: prod-sre.

laura.s: acked. i'm on it, pulling up dashboard and recent deploys. any recent config changes?

alex_m: i'm seeing a deploy to inference-gateway ~12m ago: git sha 9f3a2b4. rolling canary at 10% still. logs show repeated upstream EOF and 502 from model-backend. sample: `2027-07-15T14:18:22Z ERROR upstream request failed: EOF`

carmen: reported customer support: a handful of enterprise customers reported degraded responses. not yet widespread but getting support pings. raising priority with cs.

laura.s: initial triage: 1) spike started ~14:11 UTC 2) error mix 502/504 >500 3) latency increased for failed requests 4) traffic not much higher than normal. hypothesis: a regression in gateway->model-backend keepalive or connection pooling.

sre-oncall: taking over handoff. laura, can you capture a request id and a model-host log tail? i'll attempt a graceful scale and toggle canary.

laura.s: grabbing logs now. tail: ```
[2027-07-15T14:18:20Z] req_id=abc123 upstream=10.2.14.7: read tcp 10.2.14.7:443: connection reset by peer
[2027-07-15T14:18:21Z] req_id=abc124 upstream=10.2.14.9: EOF
```

alex_m: running quick health checks: `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=inference-gateway -o wide` shows 3/5 pods Ready, rest CrashLoopBackoff or NotReady. Model-backend nodes show increased socket errors.

eng-platform: i'm on standby, looking at node metrics. one GPU node has high iowait and some oom_kill msgs around 14:10. possible memory pressure on model-backend causing connection resets.

sre-oncall: mitigation plan (stepwise):
1) mute noisy alerting rules to avoid paging fatigue: `incident-bot mute-rule INFERENCE_GATEWAY_5XX_SPIKE 30m`
2) fail traffic away from canary: `kubectl patch svc gateway -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"canary":"false"}}}'` (will route 100% to stable)
3) scale model-backend ASG +3 instances: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize model-backend-mig --size=12`
4) restart unhealthy gateway pods: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-gateway -n prod`
5) enable fallback route to small-llm-quant for premium customers: `route: prefer=stable-small-llm on error`

laura.s: executing step 2 and 4 now. stepping canary down.

alex_m: scaling model-backend MIG now. started +3 nodes. also bumping connection_pool size in gateway config from 50 -> 80 as temporary.

carmen: notifying Sales & CS for impacted customers and opening a customer incident note. ETA for mitigation steps?

sre-oncall: ETA 6-10m for nodes to join and pods to stabilize. will update. please avoid non-essential deploys.

[14:26:35] eng-platform: new nodes joined, kubelet reports Ready. model-backend pods scheduling onto new nodes.

[14:30:12] alex_m: restarted gateway pods finished rolling restart. health checks passing for 4/5, one still restart-looping, investigating.

[14:33:04] laura.s: error rate dropping: 5m error rate now 3.1% (was 14.8%). latency back to baseline for successful requests. logs show fewer EOFs.

sre-oncall: continuing watch. enabling fallback route for premium customers now to reduce customer-visible failures. command applied.

carmen: CS updated customers A,B,C with mitigation actions and ETA. they asked for postmortem once resolved.

[14:38:07] pagerduty: Incident P12345 acknowledged by sre-oncall.

eng-platform: note — collected kernel logs from affected node, found repeated `Out of memory: Killed process` for model-server worker. looks like memory leak under heavier batch sizes.

alex_m: temporarily lowered batch size setting for model-backend to reduce memory pressure: `MODEL_BATCH_MAX=8` and redeployed model server config. monitoring.

[14:44:20] laura.s: error rate steady ~1.5% over last 5m. no new customer reports. marking incident as mitigated.

sre-oncall: moving incident to monitoring. next steps: rollback canary change to original after a postmortem, schedule model-backend memory debugging, add autoscaling policy tied to memory pressure, add defensive circuit-breaker in gateway to avoid cascading failures.

pagerduty: Incident P12345 status: Mitigated -> Monitoring.

laura.s: filing postmortem ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-9876 with timeline and actions. assigning to eng-runtime + eng-platform.

carmen: closing loop with customers and scheduling a short follow-up call for any lingering impact.

sre-oncall: thanks all. we'll keep watch for 2 hours and then close if stable. :thumbsup:
